newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia wants HK workers out before '97 handover.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia wants HK workers out before '97 handover.

text.p: Jakarta will ask some 60,000 Hong Kong people working in Indonesia to leave by June because their travel documents may not be valid after China takes over the British colony, an immigration spokesman said on Monday.
"The people, who are mostly workers, will have to leave Indonesia by June for Hong Kong, where their documents will be authorised by the Chinese government," the spokesman said.
"The people can return to Indonesia again once their documents have been authorised by the Chinese government."
The workers were originally to have left by the end of March but have been granted a three-month reprieve, an immigration spokesman said on Monday.
The spokesman said the documents held by the affected 60,000 people would no longer be valid after Hong Kong is returned to Chinese sovereignty on July 1.
"Without any recommendation from the Chinese government, the people can no longer work here," the spokesman said.

The spokesman said the people were holders of Certificates of Identity (CI), a travel document held by about 1.3 million people who have become Hong Kong permanent residents but who have no claim to a national passport issued by any country.
Most governments regard the CI as a "stateless" person's travel document. Its holders must obtain visas before travelling.

The document will eventually be replaced by a new Hong Kong passport that will be issued by the post-colonial government of the "Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR)", which will be considered a special type of Chinese national passport.
Officials in Hong Kong have said the CI might remain in use for a while after the handover as it will take time to issue new SAR passports to a large number of people.

Hong Kong's transition to Chinese rule has confused a number of governments who are anxious about possible immigration tangles. Last December Indonesia turned away more than 200 travellers from Hong Kong even though they had prior visas.
